input.note: stored as a raw little-endian float32 sidecar (`input_file`), not regenerated from the seed: torch's RNG stream is platform-dependent, so seed regeneration reproduced this matrix on the capturing Windows build but NOT on the Linux CI runner (measured sha256 62963e38fec546feda743400d392c2a53a673facccda76422505d72b34f07165 there), which made the oracle gate platform-dependent. The sidecar is 2359296 bytes (768*768*4) against the ~12 MB the same matrix cost as JSON (A-0019). The seed path remains recorded and is still checked when the sidecar is absent.

loftq_768.note: The reference schedule starts from L=R=0, so T=1 quantizes W itself and T=2 quantizes the residual left by T=1. L and R individually depend on the SVD split convention (the reference uses a symmetric sqrt(S) split), so the gate must compare the PRODUCT L@R and the quantized weight Q, never L/R elementwise.

raw_artifact.retrieval: The full elementwise arrays (W, and Q / LR product / residual at T=1 and T=2) are NOT kept in Git: 89 MB and 4.13 million lines for no review benefit. Regenerate them by cloning yxli2123/LoftQ at ae33fd4f OUTSIDE the repository and running glue/utils.py::quant_first_iter with L=R=0 for T=1, then with its own L1,R1 for T=2, on torch.manual_seed(20261009) + randn(768,768); verify against raw_artifact.sha256.
